newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds TSB sees improving LatAm conditions.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds TSB sees improving LatAm conditions.

text.p: A low inflation environment in Latin America would provide business opportunities which Lloyds TSB Group Plc would be keen to take up, its chairman Sir Brian Pitman said on Friday.
"Privatisation and other reforms have brought about changes that have been so profound that the whole character of some economies has changed," Pitman told reporters at a news conference.
The Lloyds Bank part of Lloyds TSB was heavily involved in lending to Latin American countries such as Brazil, Argentina and Mexico and suffered accordingly during the debt crisis that followed.

Earlier, it announced results for 1996 which showed it made a profit of 127 million stg from emerging market debt (which it has renamed from problem country debt) compared with a profit of 50 million in 1995.
The 1996 result included an 86 million stg net release from provisions against bad debts in the area.

Pitman said Lloyds TSB was moving to increase its retail operations in Latin America but had no specific deals in mind other than the already announced plan to buy the consumer finance business of its 50 percent-owned Banco Multiplic in Brazil.
